To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the rate of metabolism of indolequinone antiproliferative agents by recombinant NQO1 is dependent on the nature of substituent(s) on the indole ring, and that the toxicity of the quinone agents is dependent on the rate of metabolism by NQO1.
indolequinones with electron-donating groups at the 2-position of the indole ring are metabolized rapidly by NQO1 and exhibit potent cytotoxicity toward H460 cells.

indolequinone antiproliferative activity against H460 cells is correlated with the rate of metabolism by human NQO2 and that the presence of electron-withdrawing substituents on N1 of indolequinone increases its rate of metabolism by NQO1 and its antiproliferation activity toward NQO1-expressing cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel antitumor agents that target the NQO1 enzyme.
the synthesis and study of a series of indole-2-carboxamido-quinones, indole-2,3-dicarboxamido- quinones, and indole-2-aminoquinones as potential antitumor agents.
the synthesis of indolequinone antineoplastic agents.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the rate of metabolism by NQO1 is a good predictor of the cytotoxicity of indolequinone compounds toward H460 cells, and that the rate of NQO1 metabolism correlates well with the rate of metabolism of the compounds in human liver microsomes.
the rate of metabolism is a function of the electron density on C4a, and that this electron density is a function of both the substituent at C3 and the oxidation potential of the quinone.
the rate of metabolism by NQO1 is not the primary determinant of cytotoxicity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
NQO1 is an important enzyme in the activation of the indolequinone antineoplastic agents.
the rate of metabolism is dependent upon the electron-donating properties of the substituent, with the order of activity being: OMe > NH2 > OH > H.

the presence of electron-donating substituents at the 3-position, such as methoxy and methyl, enhances the rate of metabolism by NQO1, and that the rate of metabolism of indolequinone antiproliferative agents is related to their cytotoxicity toward NQO1-expressing cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a direct correlation between the rate of metabolism by NQO1 and the cytotoxicity toward the NQO1-expressing cell line.

the presence of electron-withdrawing groups on the indole ring, and the presence of an electron-withdrawing substituent on the quinone moiety, both lead to a decrease in the rate of NQO1-mediated metabolism.
the rate of reduction of indolequinone by NQO1 is dependent upon the substituents on both the indole and the quinone ring.
